G7300.d: 1. to count throughout, number , Lat. enumerare, (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. to count out, pay in ready money, Lat. numeratim solvere, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G7301.d: 1. of objects, to be quite enough for, suffice for , τινί (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; πρός τι (Xenophon Historicus): absolute to suffice, be sufficient , (Euripides) 2. impersonal, ἐξαρκεῖ it is enough for, suffices for , with dative pers., (Herdotus Historicus), attic 3. of persons, to be satisfied with, to be a match for , with dative, (Euripides):—;with participle to be content with having , (Euripides) (ML)

G7303.d: 1. to hang upon, to make dependent upon , with genitive, (Plutarch): also in Mid., (Euripides) 2. Pass., future in middle form -αρτήσομαι, perfect -ήρτημαι:—; to be hung upon, hang upon , χειρός (Euripides) 3. to depend upon, be dependent upon, be attached to , σοῦ γὰρ ἐξηρτήμεθα (Euripides) 4. of countries, to border upon , τινος (Plutarch) 5. to be hung up or exposed to view , (Thucydides) 6. perfect passive participle, with accusative rei, having a thing hung on one, be furnished with , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7304.d: 1. to begin with, make a beginning of , Lat. auctor esse, with genitive, ἐξῆρχε γόοιο (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;so in Mid., ἐξήρχετο βουλῆς (Odyssey by Homer) 2. with accusative, βουλὰς ἐξάρχων (Iliad by Homer);—;also ἐξάρχειν or ἐξάρχεσθαι παιᾶνά τινι to begin a hymn to one, address it to him, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7306.d: Lat. exhedra, a hall or arcade in the gymnasia, a sort of cloister , (Euripides) (ML)

G7310.d: 1. to unroll , (Euripides):metaphorically to unfold , Lat. explicare, (Euripides) 2. of any rapid motion, ἴχνος ἐξ. ποδός to evolve the mazy dance, (Euripides):—;hence intransitive to wheel about , (Plutarch) 3. as military term, = ἀναπτύσσειν, Lat. explicare, to extend the front by bringing up the rear men, to deploy , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. to draw off , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7311.d: 1. to vomit forth, disgorge , (Odyssey by Homer):—;metaphorically to disgorge ill-gotten gear, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. absolute to vomit, be sick , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7312.d: 1. to work out, make completely, finish off, bring to perfection , (Herdotus Historicus), attic 2. to accomplish, perform, achieve a work, (Sophocles Tragicus); κακὸν ἐξ. τινα to work him mischief, (Herdotus Historicus):—;as Pass., ἔργον ἐστὶν ἐξειργασμένον (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐπ᾽ ἐξεργασμένοισι after the deed had been done, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. to work at : as Pass., ἀγροὶ εὖ ἐξεργασμένοι well cultivated lands, (Herdotus Historicus); [ ἡ γῆ] ἐξείργασται (Thucydides) 4. to undo, destroy, overwhelm, ruin , (Herdotus Historicus):—;as Pass., ἐξειργάσμεθα we are undone , (Euripides) (ML)

G7313.d: Pass., of rivers, to empty themselves , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7316.d: 1. to creep out of , ἔκ τινος (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. absolute to creep out or forth , (Sophocles Tragicus); of an army, οὐ ταχὺ ἐξέρπει (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7318.d: 1. a searching out, search , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a finding out, invention , (Herdotus Historicus) from ἐξευρίσκω (ML)

G7319.d: 1. to stand out or project from , τινός (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. absolute to stand out, appear , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7320.d: 1. a statement, narrative , (Thucydides) 2. explanation, interpretation , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7321.d: 1. one who leads on, an adviser , Lat. auctor, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. an expounder, interpreter , of oracles, dreams, omens, and sacred customs, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G7331.d: Dep. to propitiate , (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7334.d: Dep. to ride out or away , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7341.d: of or belonging to an exit :—;as Substantive, ἐξόδιον (i.e. μέλος); the finale of a tragedy , (Plutarch): metaphorically a catastrophe , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7342.d: to build completely, finish a building , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7344.d: 1. intransitive, of a ship, to run aground or ashore , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. transitive to run (a ship) aground :—;metaphorically to drive headlong , (Euripides) (ML)

G7345.d: 1. to destroy utterly , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 2. Mid., with perfect 2 ἐξόλωλα, to perish utterly , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G7348.d: 1. attic for ἐξόπιθεν, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. as preposition with genitive, (Aristophanes Comicus) ἐξοπίσω, αδv. (ML)

G7354.d: to break out into insolence, to run riot, wax wanton , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἐξ. ἐς τόδε to come to this pitch of insolence , (Thucydides): with an adjective neuter, παντοῖα ἐξ. to commit all kinds of violence , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7357.d: 1. a bringing in, supplying , (Thucydides) 2. a bringing in to one's aid, introduction , (Thucydides) 3. a drawing on, alluring , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G7362.d: intransitive to turn back upon one, wheel round and return to the charge , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; so in Pass., (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7364.d: to have come back, to return , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G7365.d: 1. to bloom, be in flower , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. metaphorically of any thing that forms on the surface , as a salt crust, (Herdotus Historicus); the down on fruit, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: generally, to be upon the surface, shew itself, appear plainly , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. to be bright , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G7366.d: 1. from above, above , (Euripides) 2. οἱ ἐπ. men of former time , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G7374.d: 1. a commander , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. the Roman praefectus , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7376.d: 1. to be upon , with dative, (Iliad by Homer); but in Prose with preposition, ἐπὶ τοῦ καταστρώματος (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπὶ ταῖς οἰκίαις (Xenophon Historicus) 2. to be set upon , (Herdotus Historicus):—;of rewards and penalties, to be affixed or attached , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 3. of Time, to be hereafter, remain , (Odyssey by Homer); ἐπεσσόμενοι ἄνθρωποι generations to come , (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus):—;also to be at hand , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. to be set over , Lat. praeesse, τισι (Herdotus Historicus) 5. to be added, be over and above , of numbers, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7379.d: 1. to buoy up with hope, to cheat with false hopes , (Thucydides) 2. intransitive = ἐλπίζω, (Euripides) (ML)

G7382.d: 1. annual, yearly , (Herdotus Historicus): ἐπέτειοι τὴν φύσιν changeful as the seasons, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. annual, lasting for a year , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7384.d: 1. Dep. 2. to pray or make a vow to a deity, with dative, (Homer), etc.:—;with infinitive to pray to one that . . , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. :—;with accusative rei, to pray for , (Aeschulus Tragicus): also, with accusative cognate, ἐπ. λιτάς (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. to imprecate a curse upon , τί τινι (Aeschulus Tragicus); with infinitive, ἐπεύχομαι [ αὐτῷ] παθεῖν (Sophocles Tragicus): absolute to utter imprecations , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. to glory over , τινι (Iliad by Homer) 5. to boast that , with infinitive, (Homeric Hymns), etc. (ML)
